key_insight: Explicit evidence-grounding constraints improved clinical alignment in LLM-generated menstrual health summaries, but made them harder to read.
clinical_relevance: Patient-facing summaries need to preserve clinical meaning and uncertainty while remaining understandable.
method: Generated narratives from structured menstrual health records.
Combined retrieval-augmented generation with prompt-based grounding constraints.
Evaluated alignment using natural language inference, atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures.
evidence_signal: Across three LLMs and 4,500 summaries, constraints improved uncertainty preservation and generally preserved or improved faithfulness when assessed against retrieved evidence, while omission effects varied by model.
watch_item: Greater alignment came with increased reading difficulty and medical terminology, highlighting a trade-off for patient-facing implementation.
paper_title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
